s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components
key_facts: Several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
Several weeks of external deviation of the nasal septum
No significant past medical history
Left nasal mass noted on examination
Mild left-sided proptosis present
CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy showed spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells
Rare mitotic activity
No cytologic atypia

shortlist.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis in a teenage patient

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results showing spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan findings of a heterogeneous mass in the maxillary sinus with erosion of surrounding structures are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely in a teenage patient, the presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components warrants consideration of this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: The clinical presentation and imaging findings, including the location of the mass in the maxillary sinus, make this diagnosis a plausible consideration

raw.rationale: Biopsy results showing a spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells and rare mitotic activity are characteristic of a giant cell tumor, which is consistent with the clinical presentation of a mass in the maxillary sinus with erosion of surrounding bone and displacement of the inferior rectus without muscle invasion

rejected.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
rejected.why: Typically occurs in adolescent males and is highly vascular, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma
rejected.why: Usually presents with unilateral nasal obstruction and does not typically show significant multinucleated giant cells on biopsy

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Would be expected to show cytologic atypia and more aggressive behavior, which is not present in the biopsy results

rejected.label: Esthesioneuroblastoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a mass in the nasal cavity and would be expected to show neuroblastic differentiation on biopsy, which is not mentioned
